The test image displays a mango leaf with irregular, dark, soot-like blotches covering a significant portion of its surface. This is characteristic of sooty mold, a fungal growth that feeds on the honeydew secreted by insects.

My first and only reference image view was `CyberVisionAg/Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Sooty_Mould/merged/Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`. This reference image confirms the diagnosis. It shows a similar pattern of black, patchy fungal growth on the leaf surface, which strongly correlates with the visual evidence in the test image. The other potential classes have different symptoms. Anthracnose typically presents as distinct, dark, sunken lesions. Die back would show necrosis starting from the tip or edges. Powdery mildew appears as white or grayish powdery spots. The visual evidence from the test image and its strong resemblance to the sooty mould reference image make this a high-confidence prediction.
